title: Equality of the modified splittings is extra compatibility
context: Adds a comparison identity absent from the supplied context: CT54/003, 005 concerns the Hodge extension, CT16/052 a Kummer generator, and CT44/008 a Tate-module realization; none identifies these two modified Galois sections.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection]; no dedicated splitting-comparison entry
body: The centralization statements make \(\widetilde\sigma_2=\sigma_2\cdot j_2\chi\) and \(\widetilde\sigma_1=\sigma_1\cdot u\) homomorphic sections once the two extensions are properly identified. They do not force those sections to coincide: line 27 introduces the extra comparison identity from which the formula for \(\varphi\) follows. A complete argument must identify their common origin or supply the missing compatibility, since two sections of one extension generally differ by a nonabelian cocycle.

title: The analytic quotient has a standard conditional justification
context: Adds topological hypotheses and a conditional justification not supplied by CT44/008’s Tate-module subquotient or CT16/052’s Galois generator; the context contains no matching finite-dimensional analytic-quotient argument.
ledger: WG2 §2.4 #3 [unchecked plan; broad motives connection]; no dedicated analytic-quotient result
body: If \(\pi\) is profinite and \(u\) is continuous into the \(\mathbf Q_p\)-points of a finite-type algebraic group, then \(\ker u\) is closed and \(\pi/\ker u\) is topologically isomorphic to the compact, closed image \(u(\pi)\). The closed-subgroup theorem then supplies the asserted \(p\)-adic analytic structure (Glöckner, 2016, Proposition 2.3). The continuity and finite-dimensionality hypotheses must be checked; compactness alone, or passage to an unrestricted proalgebraic target, does not imply finite-dimensional analyticity.
